P1.evidence: No setter pre-qualification is evident (no setter suffix in the title, no application read back), so P1a drops out. The rep opened with small talk about being busy and went straight to the open question: 'why are we here today? What's the thing that we can potentially help you with, Anthony?' The four-part frame was never set and no frame agreement was sought.

P2.evidence: Weight was asked ('How much are you weight?') and returned 'I have no idea... I haven't weighed myself in probably 10 years'; the rep accepted that and never asked height, and age arrived only because Anthony volunteered it. Occupation surfaced unprompted ('I own coffee shops') and the desk-vs-feet question was never asked even though Anthony volunteered 'I'm always carrying boxes'. Injuries and limitations were properly screened: 'do you have any things we need to know of injuries, mobility things, anything?' and 'Any sort of stiffnesses or anything'. Health conditions, own or hereditary, were never asked. Diet was asked directly ('How is the diet looking like at the moment?') and energy was asked ('how is your energy at the moment?'), but when Anthony answered 'I don't sleep at night and I have a lot of energy' the rep replied 'Try the coffee, maybe?' and did not run the sleep check.

P3.evidence: The rep got at aesthetics obliquely — 'Do you have like an idea from when you look in the mirror? Is it something that you're happy with?' — and landed a decent good-to-great reflection: 'It sounds like it's okay, but you don't really want to be okay. You want to be good.' The bridge was run cleanly: 'physical usually has a reason behind it. You just turned 30. Is that like a part of it?' The deep question was asked twice ('What sort of impact would that have on you when you've already put it to the side for quite a few years?') but stopped at 'I'll just be happier... it's just another goal that I will be able to reach' with no further push. 'Who else does that impact?' was never asked despite a wife and a business being on the table, and nothing was driven to marriage, legacy or identity. The closing recap was a factual summary of goals rather than the 'this isn't really about the weight' reframe.

P4.evidence: Past attempts surfaced only as texture (YouTube sessions, tried the gym and hated it); the rep never asked what happened with them or why they did not stick. He did ask the root-cause question directly — 'what's like the thing that we need to fix in order to get there for you? Is it something with accountability? What's like the thing that you feel like we need to fix?' — and let Anthony name the gap himself: 'It's just like the structure, the knowledge.' The 'information isn't the problem' line was never used, which matters here because Anthony's own diagnosis was that knowledge IS the problem, and that went unchallenged.

P5.evidence: The consequence frame was not run at any point. There is no two-year question, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', and no line in the sand. The nearest thing is the rep's observation that 'so many people don't' act at 30, which invited a comparison to others rather than a cost of inaction, and Anthony deflected it with 'Well, I don't care about the others.' The call went from goals straight to the pitch with no pain built.

P6.evidence: The pre-pitch commitment attempt was a statement rather than a question — 'I don't know if you are someone here that's actually to show up and do the work' — answered with a flat 'Yeah. Okay.' and immediately followed by the presentation. The belief question was asked only after the three pillars had been delivered ('Do you feel like, if you get those three dialed in, that you're also actually going to be able to get to the aspect where you're sharper') and drew a soft 'Yeah, it sounds like it', which the rep noticed ('Sounds like it?') and then moved past anyway. The 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in' question was never asked, and the price was presented without a clear yes.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted — the rep laid out next steps ('we go over the investments. And if we make that work, then we get you started, book an onboarding meeting with Trevor') and later asked 'do you feel like it is worth 6k?' — so the phase applies. No payment was collected and no link was sent; the rep accepted the request for an email summary and rebooked. Onboarding scheduling, the agreement email and the welcome/Skool steps are downstream of payment and were never reachable.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation was attempted but weakly and out of order — the rep asked 'out of the money aspect, right? Do you feel like, yeah, Richard, this is something I want to do?' and accepted a hedged 'I mean, yes' without confirming nothing else was in the way. He then jumped straight to structuring: 'most people, they put it up front... when it comes to doing it in six times, that would become $1,200 a month.' Of the six financial-picture moves only credit score was taken ('What's your credit score, just to check?' — 720). Cash on hand, monthly surplus after bills, number of credit cards, available credit and investments were all skipped, so there was never a basis to judge whether $1,200/month was affordable. The 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place' frame was not used.

The rep did probe rather than fold immediately — 'is there like something you want to look out for, for yourself?', 'do you feel like it is worth 6k for you to get into a sharper state...', and 'By when do you feel like you can go over that and come back to me?' — and got a genuinely weak answer back ('It could be, yes'). But none of the core moves ran: no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here', no identity move. The rep also surfaced his own motive defensively ('I know many people who said they want to think about it and they never look back') which let the prospect take control — 'Don't pressure me' — after which the rep conceded and booked a week out.

'Maybe I should wait a little. A bit longer because of my finances as well' is a right-time objection in substance. No move from OD was run — no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'the only thing you can control is right now'. The rep responded 'Okay. Sure. I'll send it to you' and asked what to include in the email.

Script gap: the prospect explicitly named the sales process while it was being run on him — 'I've been exactly where you are a few years ago. I know the speech, the structure of the speech, the question, and everything... You're making me say out loud the things I want to be.' There is no scripted play for a prospect who is themselves a salesperson and calls the frame out. The rep continued running the same structure verbatim, which visibly hardened the prospect ('Don't pressure me').

notes: The discovery half was competent but shallow and the back half collapsed: Phase 5 never ran at all, so when price landed there was no cost of inaction to weigh it against, and the commitment check was skipped in favour of a hedged 'sounds like it'. Coach the sequence, not the objection handling — this call was lost at Phase 5, not at 00:23. Second priority: when a prospect answers a discovery question with 'I don't sleep at night', that is the answer to follow, not to joke past.
